script.title: How Saturn V and SLS compares in launch power
script.description: A look at the immense power generated by humanity's largest rockets. The Saturn V and Space Launch System pushed space travel to its physical limits.
script.hook_card: The most powerful machines ever built.

shots.narration: The Saturn V stood 110 metres tall and weighed about 2,900 tonnes when fully fuelled.
At liftoff, most of that mass was fuel, with the Apollo capsule making up a tiny fraction.
Its five F-1 engines produced about 34 million newtons of thrust during launch.
That immense propulsion system burned roughly 13 tonnes of propellant every single second.
Thirteen Saturn V rockets flew between 1967 and 1973, and every one succeeded.
Decades later, NASA prepared its 98-metre-tall Space Launch System for flight.
In 2022, NASA flew the Space Launch System on the Artemis I mission.
It produced about 39 million newtons at liftoff, making it more powerful than Saturn V.
